'''Arthur Derek Campbell''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|OBE|size=85%}} (27 May 1925 – 20 December 2020) was a New Zealand [[analytical chemist]]. He was a faculty member in the Department of Chemistry at the [[University of Otago]] from 1948 to 1988, becoming a [[professor emeritus]] on his retirement.

==Early life and education==
Campbell was born in [[Waimate]] on 27 May 1925, the son of Mona Sevicke Campbell (née Jones) and David Brown Campbell.<ref name="HBTQ">{{cite book |last1=Taylor |first1=Alister |last2=Coddington |first2=Deborah |authorlink1=Alister Taylor |authorlink2=Deborah Coddington |title=Honoured by the Queen – New Zealand |year=1994 |publisher=New Zealand Who's Who Aotearoa |location=Auckland |isbn=0-908578-34-2 |page=89}}</ref> He was educated at [[Waimate High School]], and then proceeded to study chemistry at the University of Otago, graduating [[Master of Science]] with second-class honours in 1948, and  [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1953.<ref name="HBTQ"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://shadowsoftime.co.nz/university5.html |title=NZ university graduates 1970–1961: Ca–Cl |website=Shadows of Time |accessdate=23 June 2019}}</ref> His doctoral thesis was titled ''Some applications of acrylonitrile''.

In 1950, Campbell married Ruth Florence Smith, and the couple went on to have three children.<ref name="HBTQ"/><ref name="Tributes"/>

==Academic and research career==
Campbell was a faculty member in the Department of Chemistry at the University of Otago from 1948 to 1988.<ref name="Calendar"/> He was appointed as an assistant lecturer in 1948, rising to become a professor in 1971, and the [[Joseph William Mellor|Mellor Professor of Chemistry]] in 1983.<ref name="HBTQ"/> He served as a member of the University Council from 1963 to 1971, dean of the Faculty of Science from 1980 to 1982, and head of the Department of Chemistry from 1983 to 1988.<ref name="HBTQ"/> When he retired in 1988, he was conferred the title of [[professor emeritus]].<ref name="Calendar">{{cite book |title=University of Otago Calendar |url=https://www.otago.ac.nz/study/otago701059.pdf |accessdate=23 June 2019 |year=2019 |publisher=University of Otago |location=Dunedin |page=114 |archive-date=14 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220314171606/https://www.otago.ac.nz/study/otago701059.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Campbell's early research centred on [[carboxylic acid derivative]]s.<ref name="Otago Heritage">{{cite web |url=http://otago.ourheritage.ac.nz/items/show/9045 |title=Arthur D. Campbell |date= |website=Otago University Research Heritage |publisher=University of Otago |accessdate=23 June 2019}}</ref> However, he became interested in organic [[microanalysis]], and developed many analytical procedures, and improved techniques for analysing perfluorinated organic compounds.<ref name="Otago Heritage"/> Campbell served as chair of the Chemical Testing Registration Advisory Committee of the Testing Laboratory Registration Council of New Zealand from 1973 to 1985.<ref name="HBTQ"/> Internationally, he was a Bureau Member of the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry]] from 1981 to 1989.<ref name="HBTQ"/> The University of Otago's Campbell Microanalytical Laboratory is named in his honour.<ref name="Otago Heritage"/>

Between 1979 and 1980, Campbell was president of the New Zealand Institute of Chemistry.<ref name="HBTQ"/>

==Later life and death==
Campbell's wife, Ruth, died in Dunedin on 18 March 2019.<ref name="Tributes">{{cite web |url=https://www.tributes.co.nz/ViewMyTribute.aspx?id=14271 |title=Ruth Florence Campbell |date= |website=Tributes Online |accessdate=23 June 2019}}</ref> Campbell died in Dunedin on 20 December 2020.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tributes.co.nz/ViewMyTribute.aspx?id=15923 |title=Arthur Derek Campbell |website=Tributes Online |access-date=13 January 2021}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
In the [[1989 Birthday Honours (New Zealand)|1989 Queen's Birthday Honours]], Campbell was appointed an [[Officer of the Order of the British Empire]], for services to science.<ref>{{London Gazette |date=17 June 1989 |supp=3 |issue=51774 |page=32}}</ref>
